question: Eight acres of good silt beside permanent water, and the camp has taken nothing off it in a generation. They call it poisoned. I do not think they mean anything precise by the word, and I do not yet have a better one.
local_knowledge: The ground was spoiled in the Shattering and will come back when it chooses to.
academic_hypothesis: Contamination from below, of the kind the Narmada rift literature describes. Untreatable without instruments nobody has.

resolutions.conclusion: The field is spoiled and will not be planted again in our lifetimes.
resolutions.revisit: The granary walls are carrying more salt than the field and something is growing out of them.

resolutions.conclusion: It is salt, weeping up from whatever opened underneath. The soil is not ruined for everything -- only for what they have been planting. The rice on the granary walls has been solving this problem unsupervised for four hundred years.

notes: The slice's proof that knowledge is help. Both readings are reasonable; only one leads to eight acres of crop, and reaching it needs botany and archaeology together.
